body.text: How do lifestyle, year-round livability and rental rules differ across Bodrum, Antalya and İzmir?

İzmir and Antalya are major metropolitan provinces with year-round universities, private hospitals, domestic business economies, and continuous winter flight schedules. Bodrum and Fethiye offer low-rise Aegean and Lycian coastal living with strong May–October demand, though many beach clubs and boutique restaurants close from November through March, leaving central towns quieter off-season.
Rental patterns mirror this divide: İzmir and Antalya sustain steady 12-month local tenant demand, whereas Bodrum and Fethiye rely heavily on summer seasonal leases and detached-villa holiday stays.
How does Türkiye's short-term rental (Airbnb) permit law affect holiday-home investors?

Under [Law No. 7464](https://mevzuat.gov.tr/anasayfa/MevzuatFihristDetayIframe?MevzuatNo=7464&MevzuatTertip=5&MevzuatTur=1), any residential stay of 100 days or fewer requires a Tourism Purpose Rental Permit from the [Ministry of Culture and Tourism](https://www.ktb.gov.tr/genel/bakanlikbelgelikonutlar.en.aspx). Detached villas avoid the unanimous apartment-building owner consent rule, making standalone coastal villas far easier to license legally than coastal apartment flats, where one objecting neighbor blocks short-term hosting.

Unlicensed hosting triggers steep 2026 revalued fines starting at [180,617 TRY per property](https://www.airroi.com/airbnb-data/turkey/regulations) and rising to 903,088 TRY and 1,806,177 TRY for repeat violations. Before buying a coastal apartment for holiday income, check whether it qualifies as a serviced residence (yüksek nitelikli konut) or pivot to a detached villa. Read our full [Türkiye short-term rental law guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/airbnb-law-turkey-2026).
Which neighborhoods are closed to foreign residence permits?

The [Presidency of Migration Management](https://en.goc.gov.tr/residence-permit-types) previously closed over 1,100 neighborhoods where foreign residents exceeded 20% of the population, including popular Antalya zones (Konyaaltı, Muratpaşa, and Alanya's Mahmutlar, Kestel, Kargıcak, and Avsallar). Although [June 2026 administrative practice eased](https://newtimeinvestment.com/en/news/residence-permit-restrictions-lifted-alanya-2026) and reopened many areas to applications, no permanent statutory repeal exists.

Because quotas can tighten again without long notice, never rely on a broker's verbal assurance. Have a licensed Turkish immigration lawyer verify the exact street address in live e-İkamet before signing. See our [Turkish residence permit (Ikamet) 2026 guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-residence-permit-2026).
What ongoing site (aidat) and property tax costs should buyers budget?

Coastal owners must budget for annual municipal property tax (Emlak Vergisi), compulsory earthquake insurance (DASK), and monthly site management fees (aidat). Because Muğla (Bodrum and Fethiye), Antalya, and İzmir are all metropolitan municipalities, the annual residential [Emlak Vergisi rate is 0.2%](https://rafetaslan.av.tr/en/property-taxes-and-hidden-costs-when-buying-real-estate-in-turkey) of the municipal assessed value, payable in March–May and by November 30.

Monthly aidat varies widely: a basic town flat costs little, whereas a gated Bodrum or Antalya resort complex with security, maintained gardens, and shared pools can cost several hundred euros monthly year-round. Run this pre-purchase cost checklist:

items: Request 12 months of aidat budgets and extraordinary repair votes from site management.
Verify the municipal assessed value (rayiç bedel) to calculate annual 0.2% [Emlak Vergisi](https://www.ronalegal.com/en/blog/property-tax-in-turkey-for-foreigners-2026-rates-valuable-housing-tax).
Obtain active DASK earthquake insurance and private coastal home insurance quotes.
Check winter heating and insulation — many older Aegean homes lack central heating.
Have an independent lawyer complete [TAPU and Iskan verification](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/tapu-verification-turkey) before paying a deposit.

faq.q: Which Turkish coastal city is best for year-round living?
faq.a: İzmir and Antalya provide the strongest year-round infrastructure, with full hospitals, international schools, and direct winter flights. Bodrum and Fethiye are quieter from November to March.

faq.q: Can I legally list a Bodrum or Fethiye villa on Airbnb in 2026?
faq.a: Yes, with a [Ministry of Culture and Tourism](https://www.ktb.gov.tr/genel/bakanlikbelgelikonutlar.en.aspx) permit, official plaque, and police guest reporting (KBS). Detached villas do not need apartment-block unanimous consent.

faq.q: What is the annual property tax rate in Bodrum, Antalya, Fethiye, and İzmir?
faq.a: All four lie in metropolitan municipalities, so the residential [Emlak Vergisi rate is 0.2%](https://rafetaslan.av.tr/en/property-taxes-and-hidden-costs-when-buying-real-estate-in-turkey) of the municipal assessed value annually.

faq.q: Are Alanya and Antalya neighborhoods still closed to residence permits in 2026?
faq.a: Administrative practice [eased in June 2026](https://newtimeinvestment.com/en/news/residence-permit-restrictions-lifted-alanya-2026) for areas like Mahmutlar and Kestel, but buyers should verify exact addresses live on e-İkamet before purchasing.

faq.q: Do I pay monthly aidat if I only visit my holiday home in summer?
faq.a: Yes. Under Turkish condominium law, aidat funds year-round shared maintenance and remains payable regardless of occupancy.
